claims.behaviour: `new ProcessButtonParameters(caption, url)` returns exactly the given caption and URL from `getCaption()` and `getUrl()`; the no-argument constructor leaves both null; `setCaption` and `setUrl` replace the values, and null is accepted everywhere.

Two `ProcessButtonParameters` are equal when the other object is of exactly the same class and both caption (`I18nText` equality) and URL are equal, with null equal to null; equal objects have equal `hashCode()`. Comparison with null or with an object of another class (including a subclass) gives false.

A new `ProcessDisplayParameters()` has a null name and an empty, modifiable button list. `getButtons()` returns the live list (adding to it changes the object); `setButtons` stores the given list object itself (null allowed, after which `getButtons()` returns null); `setName` accepts null.

The copy constructor gives the same name and a new list holding the same button objects: adding a button to the copy does not change the original's list, but the button objects are shared. A null argument throws `NullPointerException`.

`ProcessDisplayParameters` equality requires exactly the same class, equal names and equal button lists in the same order (two lists with the same buttons in different order are not equal); `hashCode()` is consistent with that. Null and other classes give false.

`ProcessDisplayParameters.Builder`: `withProcessName(key, args...)` sets the name to an `I18nText` with that key and arguments; `addButton(url, captionKey, args...)` appends a button whose URL is the first argument and whose caption is an `I18nText` of the key and arguments; both return the same builder. `build()` returns the builder's own instance, so calling `build()` twice gives the same object and later builder calls change an already built result. `new Builder(params)` starts from a copy of `params`, so building does not change `params`; a null argument throws `NullPointerException`.
`ProcessStatus` has the constants `PENDING`, `RUNNING`, `FINISHED` in that order with `getValue()` 0, 1 and 2.
`ProcessStatus.valueOf(int)` maps 0 to `PENDING`, 1 to `RUNNING` and every other number (2, 3, 99, -1, `Integer.MIN_VALUE`) to `FINISHED`; it never throws and never returns null.
The default `ProgressSink.increment()` (no arguments) calls `increment(1)` on the same sink.

In the plugin's progress tracker, `initialize(n)` sets the total to n with nothing done; a second `initialize` after a positive total throws `IllegalStateException`; a negative total throws `IllegalArgumentException`. After `initialize(0)` the sink still counts as not initialized: `increment`, `setDone` and `delegate` throw `IllegalStateException`, and `initialize` may be called again.

In the plugin's progress tracker, `increment(k)` and `setDone(k)` before initialization throw `IllegalStateException`. `increment(k)` throws `IllegalArgumentException` when k is negative or more than the units still left (units handed to delegates count as used); `setDone(k)` throws `IllegalArgumentException` when k is lower than the units already done or higher than the total. Example: after `initialize(10)`, `increment(4)` then `setDone(3)` fails, `setDone(10)` succeeds, and a further `increment(1)` fails.

In the plugin's progress tracker, `complete()` marks all units as done (percent complete becomes 100) and completes every delegate created from the sink, recursively. On a sink with no units left, including one never initialized, it does not throw.

In the plugin's progress tracker, `delegate(k)` reserves k of the sink's remaining units for a sub-task and returns a new sink that must be initialized with its own total; the sub-sink's fraction done is scaled into the k reserved units when the parent's percent complete is computed (e.g. parent total 10, delegate(5), sub-sink initialize(2) and increment(1) gives the parent 25 percent, rounded). `delegate` throws `IllegalStateException` on an uninitialized sink and `IllegalArgumentException` for a negative k or more than the units left. `setActivity` and cancellation on a delegate act on the root tracker.

In the plugin's progress tracker, `isCancelled()` is false until the tracker (or any delegate, which share the flag) is cancelled, then true. If the calling thread is interrupted, `isCancelled()` returns true, sets the cancelled flag permanently and clears the thread's interrupt status.

The default `getLong(structureId, key, def)` reads `getString(structureId, key, null)` and returns it parsed as a decimal long; it returns `def` when the string is null or not a valid long (e.g. `"abc"`, `"1.5"`, `""`, or a number beyond the long range). `"-42"` gives -42.
The default `setValue(structureId, key, long value)` calls the string `setValue` with the same structure ID and key and the decimal text of the number (e.g. -7 becomes `"-7"`).

In the plugin's property service, `setValue` with a non-blank string stores it so that `getString` returns it and `getAllKeys` contains the key; `setValue` with null, empty or whitespace-only text removes the property, after which `getString` returns the given default. Properties are scoped per structure ID: the same key under another structure ID is independent. `removeAllProperties(id)` removes all keys of that structure only; `getAllKeys` of a structure without properties is an empty set.
`new DataVersion(sig, ver)` returns `sig` from `getSignature()` and `ver` from `getVersion()` without any check (negative values allowed). `DataVersion.ZERO` has signature 0 and version 0.
`isComparable(other)` is true exactly when `other` is not null and has the same signature, regardless of version; `isComparable(null)` is false.

`isBefore(other)` for a comparable `other` is true when this version is strictly smaller (`(5,1).isBefore((5,2))` true, `(5,2).isBefore((5,2))` false). For null or a different signature it returns false when Java assertions are disabled and throws `AssertionError` when they are enabled.

`increment()` returns a new stamp with the same signature and version + 1. `increment(n)` adds n; `increment(0)` returns the very same instance; a negative n throws `IllegalArgumentException` (message `version cannot decrement`). The original stamp is never changed.

`toString()` is the signature as 8-digit zero-padded lower-case hex, a colon, then the decimal version: `new DataVersion(42, 17)` gives `0000002a:17`, `ZERO` gives `00000000:0`, signature -1 gives `ffffffff:` followed by the version.
Two `DataVersion` objects are equal when they are of exactly the same class with the same signature and version; `hashCode()` is `31 * signature + version` (e.g. (1,2) gives 33).

The `VersionedDataUpdate` constructor throws `IllegalArgumentException` (message `version must not be null`) for a null version; otherwise `getVersion()` returns the given stamp. A subclass that overrides nothing reports `isFull()` false, `isEmpty()` false and `isIncremental()` true; `isIncremental()` is always the negation of `isFull()`, also when a subclass overrides `isFull()`.
A query produced by the builder's `end()` returns null from `getQueryString()`; a query parsed from text returns that text.

For the plugin's queries, `checkRow(null, forest)` and `checkRow` of a row ID not in the forest return false, and `checkIndex` with an index outside the forest returns false; a query that fails validation for the current user returns no rows from `execute`, `executeIndices` and their unbuffered forms.
For the plugin's queries, `execute(forest)` returns the IDs of matching rows in forest order and `executeIndices(forest)` the indices of the same rows in ascending order; both return new arrays.
`StructureQueryBuilder.begin()` obtains the builder factory from the running plugin and returns its first step; when no factory is available it throws `IllegalStateException`.
The protected constructor of `StructureQueryBuilder` (and of `Head` and `Sub`) stores its first argument in the public field `and` and its second in `or`, unchanged.

`new StructureQueryBuilder.OpStep(helper)` sets the fields `in`, `equals` and `is` to the helper's inverse-composition step (the same object), `notIn`, `notEquals` and `isNot` to the helper's negated step, and `of` to the helper's composition step. `OpStep.or()` returns what the helper's `or()` returns.

The protected constructor of `StructureQueryBuilder.RelationConstraintStartStep` (and so of `StartStep`) copies the helper's nine relation steps into the public fields of the same names (`self`, `issue`, `child`, `parent`, `descendant`, `ancestor`, `prevSibling`, `nextSibling`, `sibling`) and keeps the helper; `StartStep.not()` returns what the helper's `not()` returns.
In the plugin's builder, `end()` on a builder with no constraint gives a query that matches no rows, and a query built with `all()` matches every row of the forest.
`StructureQueryConstraint.Sequence.EMPTY` is an `EmptySequence`, and `advance` of any `EmptySequence` returns false without calling the acceptor.

`StructureQueryConstraint.SimpleFilter.advance(acceptor)` takes one index from the input: if `matches` is true for it the index is passed to `acceptor.accept(int)`; it returns true after consuming an index (matching or not) and false, without calling `matches`, once the input is exhausted. Example: input 1,2,3 with `matches` true for odd numbers gives four calls returning true, true, true, false and accepts 1 and 3.

`StructureQueryConstraint.BulkFilter.advance(acceptor)` reads up to the bulk size (constructor argument, also in `myBulkSize`) indices from the input and, if it got any, calls `bulkFilter` once with them in input order and returns true; when the input is exhausted it returns false without calling `bulkFilter`. Example: 5 inputs with bulk size 2 give chunks [a,b], [c,d], [e] and then false. The list passed to `bulkFilter` is reused (cleared) between calls.

`StructureQueryConstraints.validateArgumentCount(args, min, max, messages)` returns the same message set it was given; it adds one error message when `args.size()` is below `min`, one when it is above `max`, and none when it is within the inclusive range. The error texts are localized for the current user and mention the actual and required counts.

`RestAttributeSpec.fromRestNotNull(spec)` returns an `AttributeSpec` with the spec's id, the `ValueFormat` whose format ID equals `spec.format` and the spec's params. Recognized format IDs are `html`, `text`, `json`, `jsonArray`, `number`, `boolean`, `id`, `time`, `duration` and `any`; any other value, including `order` and null, throws `IllegalArgumentException` with message `format <value> is unknown`. A null spec, or an id the `AttributeSpec` constructor rejects (blank, containing a colon, longer than 190 characters), also throws `IllegalArgumentException`.

`RestAttributeSpec.fromRest(spec)` returns null for a null spec and also returns null (instead of throwing) whenever `fromRestNotNull` would throw `IllegalArgumentException`; otherwise it returns the same result.

`RestAttributeSpec.toRest(spec)` returns a new object with `id` = the spec's ID, `format` = its format ID (e.g. `html` for `ValueFormat.HTML`) and `params` = its parameters map, except that an empty parameters map is replaced by null.

`RestAttributeSpec.fromRestCollection(c)` returns an empty list for null, otherwise a new list with each element converted as by `fromRest`, in the original order, leaving out null elements and elements that cannot be converted.
`RestAttributeSpec.toString()` is `(` id `,` format `,` params `)` with Java's default text of each field, e.g. `(summary,html,null)`.

A new `RestForestSpec` has all six fields null. Two specs are equal when the other is of the same class and `structureId`, `version`, `sQuery`, `type`, `transforms` and `title` are all equal (null equals null); `hashCode()` is consistent; null gives false.

`RestForestSpec.toString()` has the form `RestForestSpec{structureId=1, version=null, sQuery=null, type='null', transforms=null, title=null}` (type in single quotes, other fields as their own text). The static `RestForestSpec.toString(spec)` returns `null` for a null spec and `spec.toString()` otherwise.
`RestForestSpec` is deserialized by Jackson with unknown JSON properties ignored, and its JSON property names are the field names (`structureId`, `version`, `sQuery`, `type`, `transforms`, `title`).
`RestJobId` is a plain holder with one public `Long jobId` field, null in a new instance.

`RestSQuery` equality requires the same class and equal `query` and `type` (null equals null); `hashCode()` is `31 * h(query) + h(type)` with 0 for null. `toString()` is `RestSQuery{query='<query>', type='<type>'}`, e.g. `RestSQuery{query='project = A', type='jql'}`.

`RestTransformSpec` equality requires the same class and equal `module` and `params` (null equals null); the `key` field is ignored, so two specs differing only in `key` are equal and have the same hash. `hashCode()` is `31 * h(module) + h(params)` with 0 for null (as the original does).
`RestTransformSpec.toString()` is `RestTransformSpec{module='<module>', params='<params>'}` (params in quotes as the map's own text, `key` not shown).

`RestValueRequest` is a `RestJobId` (inherits `jobId`) with a public `requests` list, null when new. `RestValueRequest.ForestRowValueRequest` is a plain holder with public fields `forestSpec`, `signature` (a primitive long, 0 when new), `rows` and `attributes` (null when new).

`RestValueResponse` is a plain holder with public fields `responses`, `itemTypes` and `itemsVersion`; `RestValueResponse.ForestRowValueResponse` has `forestSpec`, `rows`, `data`, `forestVersion` and `inaccessibleRows`; `RestValueResponse.AttributeResponseData` has `attribute`, `values`, `trailMode` and `trails`. All fields are null in new instances and the JSON property names equal the field names.

A new `RestVersion` has `signature` 0 and `version` 0. `RestVersion.fromModel(v)` copies the signature and version of a `DataVersion` into a new object (null throws `NullPointerException`); `toModel()` returns a new `DataVersion` equal to `new DataVersion(signature, version)`, so a round trip gives an equal stamp.

`RestEffect.fromAppliedEffect(effect)` returns a new object whose `generatorRowId`, `external`, `description` and `reversible` fields are the effect's generator row ID, external flag, description and reversible flag. A new `RestEffect` has 0, false, null, false.

`RestEffectBatch.fromAppliedBatch(batch)` returns a new object with `batchId` = the batch's ID and `effects` = a new list holding one `RestEffect` per effect of the batch, converted as by `RestEffect.fromAppliedEffect`, in the batch's order (an empty batch gives an empty list). A null batch throws `NullPointerException`.

`new DummyRow(rowId, itemId, semantics, item)` returns the given row ID, item identity and semantics from the getters. Row ID 0 or -1 throws `IllegalArgumentException`; other values, including negative ones, are accepted.
`DummyRow.getItem(cls)` returns the stored item when it is an instance of `cls` (so `Object.class` always returns it), and null when the item is null or of another class. No access check is made.
`ItemAccessMode` has exactly the constants `NORMAL_ACCESS`, `ITEM_NOT_NEEDED` and `SKIP_ACCESS_CHECK`, in this order.

`new MissingRowException(id)` has message `row <id> is not found` (e.g. `row 42 is not found`) and `getRowId()` = id; `new MissingRowException(id, msg)` has message `msg`. It is an unchecked exception (a `StructureRuntimeException`, so a `RuntimeException`).

`RowManager.findRows(itemId)` (default) collects every row ID that the predicate form of `findRows` reports into a new array and returns an iterator over it, in the reported order; `findRows(itemId, LongConsumer)` (default) passes every reported ID to the consumer and never stops early. Both pass the item identity (null included) through unchanged.

`RowManager.collectItemIds(rows)` (default) returns an empty set for null; otherwise it scans the rows with `ITEM_NOT_NEEDED` access, skipping missing row IDs silently, and returns a set of the distinct item identities shown by the rows.

In the plugin's row manager, `createRow(itemId, semantics)` returns a new positive row ID on every call, also for the same item, and `getRow` of that ID returns a row with that item identity and semantics; `findRows(itemId)` then includes the new ID. `findRows(null)` reports nothing, and `getRow` of an ID that was never created throws `MissingRowException`.
`RowMapper.Mapping.identical(rows)` returns a mapping whose requested and mapped rows are both the given list object, whose `getMap()` is null and whose `isMapped()` is false.

`RowMapper.Mapping.mapped(requested, mapped, map)` returns a mapping that gives back exactly these three objects (not copies) from `getRequestedRows()`, `getMappedRows()` and `getMap()`; `isMapped()` is true when the map is not null.

`Mapping.createMappedResultColumn(column)` returns an empty `ValueColumn` for null and the given column itself for a mapping without map. With a map, it returns a column that, for a requested row ID, looks up the value of the mapped ID when the map has the ID as a key and of the same ID otherwise; a null row is treated as 0.
`RowRetriever.IGNORE_MISSING_ROWS` is the integers library's `LongCollector.DUMMY`, a collector that accepts and discards values.
`RowRetriever.getRow(rowId)` (default) returns `getRow(rowId, ItemAccessMode.NORMAL_ACCESS)`, propagating its `MissingRowException`.

The five-argument default `scanRows(rows, sorted, access, missing, predicate)` does nothing for null rows; otherwise it calls `getRow(id, access)` for each ID in the given order and passes the row to the predicate, stopping right after the first false. The `sorted` flag does not change this. When `getRow` throws `MissingRowException`: with a null collector the exception propagates (rows before it were already visited); with a collector the ID is added to it and the scan continues.
Shorter `scanRows` overloads use `NORMAL_ACCESS`; the forms without `sorted` pass false; `scanRows(rows, predicate)` passes a null collector, so a missing row throws `MissingRowException`.

`scanAllRows` (all forms) visits every row like `scanRows` but passes each row to a consumer and never stops early; defaults are `NORMAL_ACCESS`, unsorted and, for `scanAllRows(rows, consumer)`, a null collector (missing rows throw `MissingRowException`). Null rows visit nothing.

`scanAllExistingRows` (all forms) visits every existing row in the given order and skips missing IDs silently (it passes the discarding collector); it never throws `MissingRowException`. Forms without an access mode use `NORMAL_ACCESS`.

`reduceOverRows(rows, start, acc)` returns `start` for null or empty rows; otherwise it applies `acc.apply(row, current)` to every row in order with `NORMAL_ACCESS` and returns the final value (e.g. counting rows gives the number of IDs). A missing row throws `MissingRowException`.

`collectIssueIds(rows, [sorted,] collector)` returns the same collector. For null rows it adds nothing. Otherwise it reads rows with `ITEM_NOT_NEEDED` access, skips missing IDs, and adds the long ID of each row whose item identity is a long identity of the issue item type (`com.almworks.jira.structure:type-issue`); other rows are skipped, and an issue shown in several rows is added once per row.
`new ShallowRow(rowId, itemId, semantics)` returns these values from the getters, and `getItem` always returns null, also for `Object.class`. Row ID 0 or -1 throws `IllegalArgumentException`.

`ShallowRow.toString()` is the item identity's text with a leading `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-` removed, then `:` and the semantics: an issue identity with ID 10 and semantics 0 gives `issue/10:0`; an identity of a type without that prefix keeps its full type text. The row ID is not shown.

`SimpleRow.create(id, item, sem, resolver)` returns a checking `SimpleRow`; with a null resolver every `create` form returns a `ShallowRow`. `create(..., ItemAccessMode)` returns a `ShallowRow` for `ITEM_NOT_NEEDED`, an unchecked row for `SKIP_ACCESS_CHECK` and a checking row otherwise. `create(..., boolean skip)` returns an unchecked row for true. Every form throws `IllegalArgumentException` for row ID 0 or -1. The resulting rows return the given ID, identity and semantics.

A `SimpleRow` resolves its item on the first `getItem` call only: the checking variant calls the resolver's `resolveItem(itemId, Object.class)`, the unchecked one `resolveUnchecked(itemId)`; later calls reuse the result even for other classes. `getItem(cls)` returns the item when it is an instance of `cls` and null otherwise (including a null item). If resolution throws, the exception propagates from that call and the row is marked as resolved, so later calls return null without resolving again (as the original does).

`SimpleRow.toString()` is `SimpleRow[<rowId>:<itemId>:<semantics>]` for a checking row and `SimpleRow(unchecked)[<rowId>:<itemId>:<semantics>]` for the unchecked variant, with the item identity's full text, e.g. `SimpleRow[5:com.almworks.jira.structure:type-issue/10:0]`.

`SimpleRow.tryMakeUnchecked(row)` returns, for a checking `SimpleRow`, a new unchecked row with the same ID, identity, semantics and resolver; for an already unchecked row, a row of any other class, or null, it returns the argument itself.

`StructureRow` is an interface with the four abstract methods `getRowId()`, `getItemId()`, `getSemantics()` and `getItem(Class)` and one constant, `ROW_ZERO`: a `StructureRow.ZeroRow` whose row ID is 0, item identity is `ItemIdentity.ITEM_ZERO`, semantics is 0 and `getItem` of any class is null. Its `toString()` is `0:` followed by the item identity's text, i.e. `0:0/0`.

`StructureRows.validateForestRowId(0)` throws `IllegalArgumentException` with message `row ID must be non-zero`; `validateForestRowId(-1)` throws it with message `row ID -1 is reserved for super-root and cannot be used`; every other value (positive, -2, -100, `Long.MIN_VALUE`) passes.

`StructureRows.validateForestRowIds(list)` passes for null or a list without 0 and -1; otherwise it throws `IllegalArgumentException` for the first bad entry with the single-ID message prefixed by `[<index>] `, e.g. list 5,7,0 gives `[2] row ID must be non-zero`.

`StructureRows.withoutSuperRoot(iterator)` returns a lazy iterator over the same values with every -1 left out (1,-1,2,-1 gives 1,2); the iterable form returns an iterable whose every iterator is filtered the same way, so it can be iterated more than once.
`StructureRows.isSuperRoot(long)` is true only for -1; `isSuperRoot(StructureRow)` is true when the row is not null and its row ID is -1 (e.g. `SuperRootRow.SUPER_ROOT_ROW`), false for null.

`StructureRows.isItemType(row, type)` is true when both are non-null and the row's item type equals `type` exactly (case-sensitive). `isGenerator`, `isEffector` and `isLoopMarker` check the item types `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-generator`, `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-effector` and `com.almworks.jira.structure:type-loop-marker`; `isAutomation` is true for generator or effector rows. All are false for a null row.

`StructureRows.STARTING_TEMPORARY_ROW_ID` is -100. `isTemporary(id)` is true for -100 and lower and false for -99, -1, 0 and positive IDs. `temporaryRow(n)` returns `-100 - n` (0 gives -100, 5 gives -105) and throws `IllegalArgumentException` for a negative n.

`StructureRows.isItemVisibleForSure(row)` is true only when the row, after unwrapping any `TransientRow` wrappers, is an unchecked `SimpleRow` (made with skip-access-check); it is false for checking `SimpleRow`s, `ShallowRow`, `DummyRow`, `SuperRootRow` and null.

`StructureRows.makeShallow(row)` returns a `ShallowRow` itself unchanged and converts any other row into a new `ShallowRow` with the same ID, identity and semantics (so `getItem` becomes null). For a `TransientRow` it converts the innermost row and returns a new `TransientRow` with the outer wrapper's creator and original IDs, or the same wrapper when the innermost row is already shallow. Rows with ID 0 or -1, such as `ROW_ZERO` and `SuperRootRow.SUPER_ROOT_ROW`, make it throw `IllegalArgumentException` (as the original does).

`StructureRows.makeUnchecked(row)` turns a checking `SimpleRow` into an unchecked one (see `SimpleRow.tryMakeUnchecked`), also inside a `TransientRow` (a new wrapper with the same creator and original IDs is returned); any other row, or a wrapper around one, is returned as the same object.

`SuperRootRow` constants: `SUPER_ROOT_ROW_ID` = -1, `SUPER_ROOT_SEMANTICS` = -1, `SUPER_ROOT_INDEX` = -1, `SUPER_ROOT_DEPTH` = -1, `SUPER_ROOT_ITEM_TYPE` = `super-root`, and `SUPER_ROOT_ITEM` a long item identity with type `super-root` and ID -1 (text `super-root/-1`).
`SuperRootRow.SUPER_ROOT_ROW` returns row ID -1, item identity `SUPER_ROOT_ITEM`, semantics -1, null from `getItem` of any class, and `toString()` `super-root`. The class has no public constructor.

`new TransientRow(delegate, creatorId, originalId)` returns the delegate's row ID, item identity, semantics and `getItem` result, and the given creator and original IDs from `getCreatorId()` and `getOriginalId()`. The constructor checks nothing (a null delegate fails only when a row method is called).
`TransientRow.toString()` is `TransientRow[<rowId>:<itemId>:<semantics>:<creatorId>:<originalId>]` with the item identity's full text.

The static `TransientRow.getCreatorId(row)` and `getOriginalId(row)` return the wrapper's IDs for a `TransientRow` and 0 for any other row and for null. `getDelegate(row)` unwraps nested `TransientRow`s down to the innermost row and returns the argument itself (including null) when it is not a wrapper.

`TransientRow.replaceDelegate(row, f)`: for a non-wrapper row it returns `f(row)`, or `row` when that is null. For a wrapper it applies `f` to the innermost row and returns a new single `TransientRow` around the result with the outermost wrapper's creator and original IDs (nested wrappers collapse into one); when `f` returns null or the same innermost object it returns the original wrapper.

`AttributeSensitivityMode` has `STANDARD`, `STRICT`, `PERMISSIVE` in this order with `getCode()` 0, 1 and 2. `valueOf(int)` returns the mode with that code and throws `IllegalArgumentException` for any other number, with message `<n> is not a valid sensitivity mode code` (e.g. `3 is not a valid sensitivity mode code`).

`AutoSwitchStrategy` has `AUTOSWITCH_OFF` (code `off`), `STRUCTURE_WITH_ISSUE` (`withIssue`) and `DEFAULT_STRUCTURE` (`default`) in this order; `PLUGIN_DEFAULT_AUTOSWITCH_STRATEGY` is `STRUCTURE_WITH_ISSUE`.

`AutoSwitchStrategy.fromStringCode(code)` returns the constant whose code equals the argument exactly (case-sensitive: `withIssue` matches, `WITHISSUE` and `withissue` do not) and null for null or an unknown code. It never throws.

`new ImmutableAttributeSensitivitySettingsBean(mode, specs)` returns `mode` from `getSensitivityMode()` (null is not checked) and from `getNonSensitiveAttributes()` an unmodifiable set copy of `specs` (duplicates collapse, later changes to `specs` have no effect, and modifying the set throws `UnsupportedOperationException`). A null collection throws `NullPointerException`.
`ImmutableAttributeSensitivitySettingsBean.DEFAULT` has mode `STANDARD` and an empty set of non-sensitive attributes.

The default permission shortcuts of `StructureConfiguration` call the generic methods with fixed `CoreAppPermissions` constants: `isEnabledForAnyone`, `getEnabledPermissionSubjects`, `setEnabledForAnyone` and `setEnabledPermissionSubjectsEncoded` use `USE`; the `Create`/`Creator` and `isStructureCreationAllowed` methods use `CREATE_STRUCTURE`; the `Synchronization` methods and `isSynchronizationAllowed` use `SYNCHRONIZATION`; the `Automation` methods and `isAutomationAccessAllowed` use `AUTOMATION`. Results of the generic methods are returned unchanged.

The default `setPickedProjectIds(LongIterable)` and `setPickedProjectIds(Collection<Long>)` call the string form with the IDs as a comma-separated decimal list in iteration order without spaces (10, 20, 30 gives `10,20,30`); an empty input gives `""` and null gives `""`.

The default `setPermissionSubjects(permission, subjects)` calls `setPermissionSubjectsEncoded(permission, text)` where text is each subject's `toEncodedString()` joined with commas in iteration order; null subjects give `""`.

In the plugin's configuration with nothing stored, `isEnabledForAllProjects()` is true, `isAllowedForAnyone` is true for every known permission, `getPermissionSubjects` is empty, `getPickedProjectIds()` is empty, `getDefaultStructureId` is 0 for any project and `getAttributeSensitivitySettings()` is mode `STANDARD` with no attributes. `isProjectEnabled(null)` is false.

In the plugin's configuration, `setDefaultStructureId(null, id)` sets the global default (null stores 0); `setDefaultStructureId(project, id)` sets a project default and a null ID removes it. `getDefaultStructureId(project)` returns the project's own default, else the global default, else 0; `isDefaultStructureSetForProject` is true only when the project has its own default.

In the plugin's configuration, `isAllowed(permission, null)` is false. For a user who passes `isStructureAvailable`, it is true when the permission is granted to anyone, when the user is a Jira administrator (with the administrator bypass on, the default), or when a stored permission subject matches the user; otherwise false. `isStructureAvailable` is false when the plugin is enabled for no project.

In the plugin's configuration, `getConfigurationScopeQuery()` is null and `addConfigurationScopeClause` adds nothing when the plugin is enabled for all projects; otherwise the clause restricts the project to the enabled project IDs (joined with AND; a new builder is made for null), and with no enabled project it restricts to project ID 2147483647.

`StructurePage` constants in order and their `getId()`: `STRUCTURE_BOARD` `structure`, `STRUCTURE_BOARD_WITH_DETAILS` `structure-with-details` (deprecated), `ISSUE_VIEW` `issue`, `PROJECT_TAB` `project`, `COMPONENT_TAB` `component`, `VERSION_TAB` `version`, `ISSUE_NAVIGATOR` `navigator`, `GADGET` `gadget`, `GREENHOPPER_TAB` `greenhopper`. Jackson writes a page as its ID string and reads it back through `forId`.
`StructurePage.forId(id)` returns the page with exactly this ID (case-sensitive: `issue` matches, `ISSUE` does not) and null for null or an unknown ID.
`StructurePage.enumSet(pages)` returns null for a null or empty collection; otherwise a new `EnumSet` with the given pages (duplicates collapse). A null element throws `NullPointerException`.

A new `UISettingsBean()` has no strategy for any page, both flags null and `isAnythingSet()` false. `setAutoSwitchStrategy(page, s)` stores `s` for that page only (other pages stay null), null removes it, and it returns the same bean; a null page throws `NullPointerException` (message `page is null`). `setAutoCollapseStructurePanel` and `setKeepStructureWhileNavigating` store their `Boolean` as is (null unsets). `isAnythingSet()` is true when any page strategy or either flag is set, including a flag set to false.

`new UISettingsBean(other)` copies the auto-switch strategy of every page and the auto-collapse flag from `other`, but not the keep-while-navigating flag, which stays null (as the original does); `new UISettingsBean(null)` is the same as the no-argument constructor.
